items.titleEn: Gold, silver soften as markets price in December Fed hike risk - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were lower after the close Monday as a firmer U.S. dollar, renewed oil strength and elevated Treasury-yield risk offset safe-haven demand tied to the Strait of Hormuz and the U.S.-Iran conflict. At the time of writing, spot gold was trading near $4,168.90 an ounce, down 0.59%, while spot silver was trading at $60.120, down 0.96% on the session. The latest price action is less about an immediate October Fed move and more about whether this week’s inflation data revives the December tightening path. Markets were pricing roughly a 17% chance of an October hike and an 87.7% probability of at least one hike by December after softer recent U.S. data lowered near-term hike risk but oil-driven inflation concerns kept year-end policy risk alive. September CPI is due Wednesday, followed by PPI and retail sales Thursday. This setup has left gold exposed to the dollar and real-yield channel, even as ETF demand and central-bank buying remain supportive beneath the market.

items.titleEn: Gold defies multi-decade high bond yields, but Q4 headwinds remain – Invesco
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The gold market continues to face significant headwinds from persistent inflation, rising interest rates and higher bond yields; however, the precious metal has demonstrated remarkable resilience, ending the third quarter with solid gains even as U.S. Treasury yields climbed to multi-decade highs. According to one investment firm, these competing forces are expected to remain important drivers of gold prices through the final three months of the year. In their latest quarterly outlook, market analysts at Invesco said that although higher bond yields could continue to weigh on gold prices in the fourth quarter, structural demand from central banks and renewed investor interest in gold-backed exchange-traded products (ETPs) should continue to provide long-term support. The analysts noted that gold ended September at $4,157 an ounce, representing a gain of 3.7% during the third quarter. The positive performance came despite a sharp selloff in global bond markets that pushed longer-dated U.S. Treasury yields to their highest levels in more than two decades.
